name: List.iterate.eq_def
script:

have h_main : ∀ {α : Type u_1} (f : α → α) (a : α) (x : ℕ), List.iterate f a x = match x with | 0 => [] | n.succ => a :: List.iterate f (f a) n := by

name: Finset.Iic_toDual
script:
intro α inst inst_1 a
have h_main : Finset.Iic (OrderDual.toDual a) = Finset.map OrderDual.toDual.toEmbedding (Finset.Ici a) := by
  apply Finset.ext
  intro x
  simp only [Finset.mem_Iic, Finset.mem_map, Finset.mem_Ici]
  constructor
  · -- Prove the forward direction: if x ≤ a, then there exists y ≥ a such that (y : OrderDual α) = (x : OrderDual α)
    intro hx
    have h₁ : a ≤ x := by simpa [OrderDual.le_def] using hx
    refine' ⟨x, _⟩
    <;> simp_all [OrderDual.le_def]
    <;>
    aesop
  · -- Prove the reverse direction: if there exists y ≥ a such that (y : OrderDual α) = (x : OrderDual α), then x ≤ a
    intro hx
    rcases hx with ⟨y, hy₁, hy₂⟩
    have h₁ : a ≤ y := by simpa [OrderDual.le_def] using hy₁
    have h₂ : (y : OrderDual α) = (x : OrderDual α) := by simpa using hy₂
    have h₃ : x ≤ a := by
      simp_all [OrderDual.le_def]
      <;>
      aesop
    exact h₃
exact h_main

name: Subfield.closure_le
script:
intro K inst s t
have h_main : Subfield.closure s ≤ t ↔ s ⊆ (↑t : Set K) := by
  constructor
  · -- Prove the forward direction: if `Subfield.closure s ≤ t`, then `s ⊆ (↑t : Set K)`
    intro h x hx
    have h₁ : x ∈ Subfield.closure s := by
      apply Subfield.subset_closure
      exact hx
    have h₂ : x ∈ (t : Set K) := by
      -- Since `Subfield.closure s ≤ t`, we can use the fact that `x` is in `Subfield.closure s` to show it is in `t`
      have h₃ : Subfield.closure s ≤ t := h
      exact h₃ h₁
    simpa using h₂
  · -- Prove the backward direction: if `s ⊆ (↑t : Set K)`, then `Subfield.closure s ≤ t`
    intro h
    have h₁ : ∀ x, x ∈ Subfield.closure s → x ∈ (t : Set K) := by
      intro x hx
      -- Since `s ⊆ (↑t : Set K)`, we can use the fact that `x` is in `Subfield.closure s` to show it is in `t`
      have h₂ : x ∈ Subfield.closure s := hx
      have h₃ : x ∈ (t : Set K) := by
        -- Use the property of `Subfield.closure` and the fact that `s ⊆ (↑t : Set K)`
        have h₄ : ∀ y, y ∈ s → y ∈ (t : Set K) := by simpa using h
        have h₅ : x ∈ Subfield.closure s := hx
        -- Use the property of `Subfield.closure` and the fact that `s ⊆ (↑t : Set K)`
        exact Subfield.closure_subset t h₅
      exact h₃
    -- Convert the result to the desired form
    have h₂ : Subfield.closure s ≤ t := by
      intro x hx
      exact h₁ x hx
    exact h₂
exact h_main

name: Polynomial.cyclotomic.eval_apply_ofReal
script:
intro q n
have h_main : Polynomial.eval (↑q) (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℂ) = Polynomial.eval (↑q) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℝ)) := by
  have h₁ : Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℂ = Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℝ) := by
    -- Prove that the cyclotomic polynomial over ℂ is the image of the cyclotomic polynomial over ℝ under the algebra map
    have h₂ : Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℂ = Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℝ) := by
      -- Use the fact that the coefficients of the cyclotomic polynomial are integers and hence real numbers
      norm_cast
      <;> simp [Polynomial.cyclotomic, Polynomial.map_def]
      <;> ring_nf
      <;> simp_all [Complex.ext_iff, Complex.I_mul_I]
      <;> field_simp [Complex.ext_iff, Complex.I_mul_I]
      <;> simp_all [Complex.ext_iff, Complex.I_mul_I]
      <;> ring_nf
      <;> norm_num
    exact h₂
  rw [h₁]
  <;> simp [Polynomial.eval_map]

have h_final : Polynomial.eval (↑q) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℝ)) = ↑(Polynomial.eval q (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℝ)) := by
  -- Use the property of polynomial evaluation under algebra homomorphisms
  simp [Polynomial.eval_map, Polynomial.eval_C]
  <;> norm_cast

have h_result : Polynomial.eval (↑q) (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℂ) = ↑(Polynomial.eval q (Polynomial.cyclotomic n ℝ)) := by
  rw [h_main]
  rw [h_final]
  <;> simp_all
  <;> norm_cast

exact h_result

name: UniqueAdd.of_card_le_one
script:
intro G _ A B hA_nonempty hB_nonempty hA_card_le_one hB_card_le_one
have hA_card_eq_one : A.card = 1 := by
  have h₁ : A.Nonempty := hA_nonempty
  have h₂ : A.card ≤ 1 := hA_card_le_one
  have h₃ : A.card ≥ 1 := by
    apply Finset.card_pos.mpr
    exact h₁
  have h₄ : A.card = 1 := by
    omega
  exact h₄

have hB_card_eq_one : B.card = 1 := by
  have h₁ : B.Nonempty := hB_nonempty
  have h₂ : B.card ≤ 1 := hB_card_le_one
  have h₃ : B.card ≥ 1 := by
    apply Finset.card_pos.mpr
    exact h₁
  have h₄ : B.card = 1 := by
    omega
  exact h₄

obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := Finset.card_eq_one.mp hA_card_eq_one
obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := Finset.card_eq_one.mp hB_card_eq_one
refine' ⟨a, _⟩
have h₁ : a ∈ A := by
  rw [ha]
  simp
refine' ⟨b, _⟩
have h₂ : b ∈ B := by
  rw [hb]
  simp
constructor
· -- Prove that (a, b) is in A × B
  exact Finset.mem_product.mpr ⟨h₁, h₂⟩
· -- Prove the uniqueness part of UniqueAdd
  intro y hy
  have h₃ : y.1 = a := by
    simp_all [Finset.card_eq_one]
    <;> aesop
  have h₄ : y.2 = b := by
    simp_all [Finset.card_eq_one]
    <;> aesop
  simp_all [Prod.ext_iff]
  <;> aesop

name: Matroid.IsStrictMinor.ne
script:
intro α M N h
have h₁ : M ≤ N := by
  -- Use the given inequality `N <m M` to derive `M ≤ N`
  exact le_of_lt h

have h₂ : ¬(N ≤ M) := by
  intro h₃
  -- If both `M ≤ N` and `N ≤ M`, then `M = N`
  have h₄ : M = N := by
    -- Use the antisymmetry of the order relation to conclude `M = N`
    exact le_antisymm h₁ h₃
  -- Substitute `M = N` into the inequality `N <m M` to get a contradiction
  rw [h₄] at h
  -- Simplify the inequality to show that it leads to a false statement
  simp_all [lt_irrefl]
  <;> aesop

have h₃ : N ≠ M := by
  intro h₄
  -- Assume `N = M` and derive a contradiction.
  apply h₂
  -- Use the assumption `N = M` to show `N ≤ M`.
  rw [h₄]
  <;> exact le_refl M

exact h₃

name: NumberField.abs_discr_gt_two
script:
intro K inst inst_1 h₁
have h₂ : 2 < |(NumberField.discr K : ℤ)| := by
  -- Use the fact that the discriminant of a number field is non-zero and its absolute value is at least 4.
  have h₃ : NumberField.discr K ≠ 0 := by
    -- Prove that the discriminant is not zero because the field has characteristic zero.
    exact NumberField.discrepancy_ne_zero (by simpa using inst_1.ne_zero)
  have h₄ : |(NumberField.discr K : ℤ)| ≥ 4 := by
    -- Use the fact that the absolute value of the discriminant is at least 4 for any number field.
    have h₅ : (NumberField.absDiscr K : ℤ) ≥ 4 := by
      -- Prove that the absolute value of the discriminant is at least 4.
      have h₆ : NumberField.absDiscr K ≥ 4 := by
        -- Use the fact that the absolute value of the discriminant is at least 4 for any number field.
        exact NumberField.abs_discr_ge_four (by simpa using inst_1.ne_zero)
      exact_mod_cast h₆
    have h₇ : |(NumberField.discr K : ℤ)| = (NumberField.absDiscr K : ℤ) := by
      -- Prove that the absolute value of the discriminant is equal to the absolute value of the discriminant.
      simp [abs_of_nonneg, Int.natCast_nonneg, NumberField.abs_discr_pos]
    rw [h₇]
    exact h₅
  have h₈ : 2 < |(NumberField.discr K : ℤ)| := by
    -- Prove that the absolute value of the discriminant is greater than 2.
    omega
  exact h₈
simpa using h₂

name: isSelfAdjoint_map
script:
intro F R S inst inst_1 inst_2 inst_3 inst_4 f x
have h₁ : ∀ (r : R), r * = r := by
  exact fun r => inst_4 trivial r

have h₂ : (f x) * = f (x *) := by
  -- Use the property of StarHomClass to relate the star operation on S with F and R.
  have h₂₁ : ∀ (a : F) (r : R), a * r = a r * := by
    intro a r
    exact inst_3.map_mul a r
  -- Apply the above property to f and x to get (f x) * = f (x *)
  have h₂₂ : (f x) * = f (x *) := by
    calc
      (f x) * = f x * := by simp [h₁]
      _ = f (x *) := by
        -- Use the property of StarHomClass to relate the star operation on S with F and R.
        have h₂₃ : ∀ (a : F) (r : R), a * r = a r * := by
          intro a r
          exact inst_3.map_mul a r
        -- Apply the above property to f and x to get (f x) * = f (x *)
        have h₂₄ : f * x = f x * := by simp [h₁]
        simpa [h₁] using h₂₃ f x
  exact h₂₂

have h₃ : (f x) * = f x := by
  calc
    (f x) * = f (x *) := h₂
    _ = f x := by rw [h₁ x]

have h₄ : IsSelfAdjoint (f x) := by
  -- Use the definition of `IsSelfAdjoint` to show that `(f x) * = f x`.
  rw [IsSelfAdjoint]
  <;> simpa using h₃

exact h₄

name: le_iInf_mul
script:
intro α ι inst inst_1 mul_left_mono mul_right_mono u v
have h_main : (∫ i, u i) * ∫ i, v i ≤ ⨅ i, u i * v i := by
  -- Use the fact that the infimum of a product is less than or equal to the product of the infima
  have h₁ : ∀ i, u i * v i ≥ (∫ j, u j) * ∫ j, v j := by
    intro i
    have h₂ : u i ≥ ∫ j, u j := by
      exact le_ciInf (by infer_instance) (fun j => by simp [le_refl])
    have h₃ : v i ≥ ∫ j, v j := by
      exact le_ciInf (by infer_instance) (fun j => by simp [le_refl])
    calc
      u i * v i ≥ (∫ j, u j) * ∫ j, v j := by
        -- Use the fact that multiplication is monotonic
        have h₄ : u i ≥ ∫ j, u j := h₂
        have h₅ : v i ≥ ∫ j, v j := h₃
        calc
          u i * v i ≥ (∫ j, u j) * ∫ j, v j := by
            -- Use the fact that multiplication is monotonic
            exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h₄ (by simpa using h₅)
          _ = (∫ j, u j) * ∫ j, v j := by rfl
      _ = (∫ j, u j) * ∫ j, v j := by rfl
  -- Use the fact that the infimum of a product is less than or equal to the product of the infima
  have h₂ : (∫ i, u i) * ∫ i, v i ≤ ⨅ i, u i * v i := by
    calc
      (∫ i, u i) * ∫ i, v i = (∫ i, u i) * ∫ i, v i := rfl
      _ ≤ ⨅ i, u i * v i := by
        -- Use the fact that the infimum of a product is less than or equal to the product of the infima
        exact ciInf_le (by infer_instance) fun i => h₁ i
  exact h₂
simpa using h_main

name: Metric.infEDist_eq_top_iff
script:
intro α inst s x
have h_imp : Metric.infEDist x s = ⊤ → s = ∅ := by
  intro h
  by_contra h₁
  -- Assume s is not empty, so there exists some y ∈ s
  have h₂ : s.Nonempty := Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr h₁
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := h₂
  have h₃ : dist x y < ⊤ := by
    -- The distance from x to y is finite and less than ⊤
    exact lt_of_le (dist_nonneg _) (by simp [top_eq])
  have h₄ : Metric.infEDist x s ≤ dist x y := by
    -- The infimum of distances from x to points in s is at most the distance to y
    apply Metric.inf_edist_le hy
  have h₅ : Metric.infEDist x s < ⊤ := by
    -- Since Metric.infEDist x s ≤ dist x y and dist x y < ⊤, we get Metric.infEDist x s < ⊤
    calc
      Metric.infEDist x s ≤ dist x y := h₄

    intro h

  · -- Prove the backward direction: if s = ∅, then Metric.infEDist x s = ⊤
    intro h

name: MeasurableSpace.measurableSet_bot_iff
script:
intro α s
have h₁ : MeasurableSet s → s = ∅ ∨ s = Set.univ := by
  intro h
  by_cases h₂ : s = ∅
  · exact Or.inl h₂
  · -- If s ≠ ∅, we need to show that s = univ
    have h₃ : s = Set.univ := by
      -- Use the fact that if a set is measurable and not empty, it must be the whole space
      apply Set.eq_univ_of_forall
      intro x
      have h₄ : MeasurableSet s := h
      have h₅ : x ∈ s ∨ x ∉ s := by by_cases h₆ : x ∈ s <;> [exact Or.inl h₆; exact Or.inr h₆]
      cases h₅ with
      | inl h₅ =>
        -- If x ∈ s, then we are done
        simp_all
      | inr h₅ =>
        -- If x ∉ s, we need to derive a contradiction
        have h₆ : MeasurableSet (sᶜ) := by
          apply MeasurableSet.compl
          exact h
        have h₇ : x ∈ sᶜ := by simpa using h₅
        have h₈ : MeasurableSet s := h
        -- Use the fact that if a set is measurable and its complement is also measurable, then it must be the whole space or empty
        have h₉ : MeasurableSet (s ∩ {x}) := by
          apply MeasurableSet.inter h₈
          exact mea
        have h₁₀ : x ∈ s ∩ {x} ↔ False := by
          constructor <;> intro h₁₀ <;>
            simp_all [Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
          <;> aesop
        -- Use the fact that if a set is measurable and its complement is also measurable, then it must be the whole space or empty
        have h₁₁ : MeasurableSet (s ∩ {x}) := by
          apply MeasurableSet.inter h₈
          exact mea
        simp_all [Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
        <;> aesop
    exact Or.inr h₃
have h₂ : s = ∅ ∨ s = Set.univ → MeasurableSet s := by
  intro h
  cases h with
  | inl h =>
    rw [h]
    exact measurableSet_empty
  | inr h =>
    rw [h]
    exact measurableSet_univ
have h₃ : MeasurableSpace α := by
  infer_instance
constructor
· -- Prove the forward direction: if s is measurable, then s = ∅ or s = univ
  intro h
  exact h₁ h
· -- Prove the reverse direction: if s = ∅ or s = univ, then s is measurable
  intro h
  exact h₂ h
